Something that happens yearly (and weekly) in fantasy, is the overreaction to 1 week of poor WR production. 

WR usage/production is extremely volatile by nature, and there's generally well less than 10 WRs in the NFL on a yearly basis that will not fall victim to weeks of minimal usage, the truly best of the best (Puka, JSN types). Just 1 WR had 5+ targets in every game last year, and only a handful more did so in 75%+ of their games.

Guys like Parker Washington (who had earned the 5th highest target share in the NFL coming into this week), or a Josh Downs (who was 13th in this regard), are not all of a sudden shaky fantasy assets/WRs because they did not produce in Week 4. That is just the nature of the position.

If we see usage declining over multiple weeks, then we can start to worry. But guys like this who are clearly talented and have shown very capable of earning targets/producing are great buy lows coming off this weeks.

Chris Olave Over 85.5 Receiving Yards

50❤️ For My NFL Play Of The Day

Monday night lights, a division rival in the building, and an Atlanta secondary without its best corner make this a stage built for Chris Olave. He's gone over this number in every game this season, posting 182 in Detroit, 86 in Baltimore, and 107 against Las Vegas, after closing last year with 148 and 119. At 12 targets a game, the offense runs through him, and Tyler Shough keeps finding him.

On The Season Olave Is Averaging.

-125 Receiving Yards Per Game
-12 Targets Per Game
-10.4 Yards Per Target
-25% Team Target Share

Atlanta ranks 30th in the league in receiving yards allowed to wide receivers, giving up 201.3 yards per game to the position, which makes this a favorable matchup for the over. Their scheme closes the middle of the field and leaves receivers one on one outside, and with A.J. Terrell on IR, the corner who made that work is no longer out there.

Last 3 WRs Vs Atlanta.

-Matthew Golden (GB) 100 Receiving Yards
-Tetairoa McMillan (CAR) 101 Receiving Yards
-Michael Pittman (PIT) 58 Receiving Yards

Green Bay showed the blueprint in Atlanta's first game without Terrell, with Golden going for 100 and Christian Watson adding 96 by beating that outside coverage. The Falcons also have the league's best run defense at 47.7 rush yards allowed per game, so New Orleans has every reason to put the ball in the air, and Olave has been Shough's top option against man coverage.
